primary_claim: Group SAEs, which use an L1/L2 group-sparsity penalty to encourage latents to jointly span multi-dimensional feature subspaces, learn some semantically related latent groups on synthetic circle data and GPT-2 layer-7 activations, but fail to cleanly avoid feature splitting/duplication and do not clearly outperform a normal SAE plus post-hoc clustering, leading the authors to consider the overall research direction unpromising.

effect.metric: explained variance and CE loss at matched sparsity (Group SAE vs ReLU SAE, GPT-2 layer 7)
effect.value: group SAEs showed slightly higher explained variance and CE loss score than ReLU SAEs at the same sparsity, and lower max intra-group cosine similarity (less apparent feature splitting), but with high feature duplication

stated_future_work: reassign groups periodically based on Jaccard similarity (idea considered worth trying but never attempted)
extend the consecutive-feature grouping idea using a decaying 'neighbor affinity' function between active points (untried)
limitations_stated: not clear if dictionary learning is the right tool for the job; there may be many more feature manifolds than concepts

not entirely clear how to measure success, since it's hard to distinguish true multi-dimensional features from merely correlated 1D features, and only a few ground-truth examples (e.g. circular features) are available
strong baselines like Matryoshka SAEs and various clustering methods might be hard to beat
gated and topk Group SAE variants did not show the same improvement in variance explained at matched sparsity, with topk performing especially badly
high feature duplication makes it hard to draw strong conclusions from the reduced max intra-group cosine similarity
quote: These results aren't exactly "negative" in that they fail at some task, but rather "negative" in that they don't seem to accomplish anything useful.
